markdown:
# Can I reach you at 2am?

You can call at 2am. We can't yet promise a person will answer at that hour, because our actual overnight answer rate isn't measured in the data behind this site.

## What happens at night

- Our current after-hours staffing and answering setup isn't documented in the sources here. We won't guess at it.
- Our planning model assumes some night calls go unanswered today. It treats about 12% of calls as after-hours and estimates that 35% of those are lost (est.) (Voice AI research).
- An AI voice agent that answers and books overnight is under evaluation. Vendors report booking rates of 70% overall and 90% when schedule capacity is open. Those figures are self-reported and unaudited, so read them as ranges, not promises (Voice AI research).

## When night calls come in

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Off-hours share of HVAC calls, June | 14.1% | Punctual Pros demand model |
| Off-hours share of HVAC calls, October | 9.8% | Punctual Pros demand model |
| Peak off-hours window | 5–9 pm local | Punctual Pros demand model |
| After-hours calls lost | 35% (est.) | Voice AI research |

- Night demand matters in winter here. About 241k core Central PA households heat with oil or propane (Punctual Pros market profile). A no-heat call can come at any hour.
- The demand model doesn't break out 2am specifically. Call logs by hour would answer that.

## What would settle this

- Hour-by-hour inbound call and answer data from our dispatch system, ServiceTitan, for the past 12 months.
- The share of 2am calls that end in a booked job versus voicemail or a hang-up.

The model puts unanswered after-hours calls at about $390,000 a year of recoverable jobs (est.). That sits inside a $1.4M missed-call estimate against roughly $22M of revenue (est.) (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings). Overnight coverage is a revenue question, not just a service courtesy.

## Next actions

1. **Measure the gap.** Pull 12 months of call logs by hour from ServiceTitan. Calculate the real overnight answer and booking rates and replace the modelled 35% loss figure.
2. **State our hours plainly.** Document how after-hours calls are handled today and publish that on this site so callers know what to expect at 2am.
3. **Test an overnight voice agent.** Pilot it at one site this heating season. Compare its booking rate against the 42% typical human rate (Voice AI research).
4. **Recalibrate the model.** Feed the pilot results back into the demand model's off-hours assumptions before the summer peak.
